claims.title: Prefix-matched redirect URI lets an attacker obtain authorization codes
claims.description: An attacker can initiate authorization for a member against `process:authorization-server` using a redirect URI that merely begins with a partner's registered URI. The authorization server then returns the authorization code over `flow:entity:member>entity:partner-app>return-with-authorization-code` to the attacker-controlled matching destination. The attacker can exchange the ten-minute code for bearer access and refresh tokens, enabling subsequent access to `process:rewards-api` as the consenting member. This is disclosure of the authorization code and resulting credentials, not a finding about how those credentials are later used.

quotes.text: the authorization server accepts any redirect URI that starts with it
An authorization code stays valid for ten minutes.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because an outside attacker needs a crafted URI matching a partner registration and a member authorization, but prefix matching makes that attack practical. Impact is high because the code returned by `process:authorization-server` can be exchanged for bearer credentials that reach the `financial` and `pii` handling `process:rewards-api`.

mitigations.detail: Require an exact, pre-registered redirect URI match at `process:authorization-server`; reject prefix, wildcard, and normalization-ambiguous matches.

mitigations.summary: Bind authorization responses to the legitimate client session
mitigations.detail: Require PKCE for public clients and bind authorization requests to a high-entropy state value validated by the receiving client.

claims.title: Identity-database traffic may expose password hashes and refresh tokens in transit
claims.description: `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` carries member accounts, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents between `process:authorization-server` and `store:identity-database`, but its `encryption_in_transit` attribute is unknown. If transport protection is absent or terminates before this segment, an attacker able to observe the cloud-internal path can intercept those credentials and PII. Stolen refresh tokens and codes can then be used to obtain access tokens for calls to `process:rewards-api`. This draft is conditional on resolving the unknown transport-control attribute.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker needs an on-path position inside `boundary:rewards-cloud` and the flow's encryption state is unverified. Impact is high because the flow carries credentials and PII for `store:identity-database`, including reusable refresh tokens and password hashes.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encrypted database transport
mitigations.detail: Establish the transport posture for `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` and require TLS with certificate validation, preferably mTLS, for the full application-to-database hop.

mitigations.summary: Limit credential exposure on the database channel
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived, rotated refresh tokens and avoid returning or replicating credential material beyond the fields needed for each database operation.

claims.title: Unverified ledger transport may disclose members' balances and transactions
claims.description: `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points` carries balances and points transactions between `process:rewards-api` and `store:points-ledger`, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that internal database segment is not protected, an attacker with an on-path foothold can intercept financial records for members whose requests are processed. The observed balances and transaction history can be used to target members and correlate later activity at the internet-facing rewards API. This is conditional on the unknown transport control, not an assertion that encryption is absent.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because observation requires an internal on-path position and the encryption state of the ledger connection is unknown. Impact is high because `store:points-ledger` contains every member's balances and points transactions and is tagged `financial` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.detail: Set and verify TLS, ideally mutual TLS, for `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points`, including any proxy or service-mesh segment.

claims.title: Unverified log-shipping transport may expose bearer tokens
claims.description: `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` sends every received request and its headers from `process:rewards-api` to `store:api-log-store`; the model records `encryption_in_transit` as unknown. If this segment lacks effective transport encryption, an on-path attacker can intercept logged bearer access tokens together with request-associated PII and financial activity. Possession of a captured bearer token enables later access to `process:rewards-api` until the token expires. This draft is conditional on the unresolved transport state.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker needs an internal on-path position and `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. Impact is high because the transmitted log records include bearer credentials, which can be replayed against the internet-facing `process:rewards-api`, as well as PII and financial request data.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate log delivery
mitigations.detail: Verify and require TLS with peer validation for `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log`.
Redact Authorization headers and tokens at `process:rewards-api` before constructing log events, so a transport failure cannot expose replayable credentials.

claims.title: Unverified support-console database transport may reveal account-closure data
claims.description: `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts` has unknown `encryption_in_transit` and carries account-closure information to `store:identity-database`. If this connection is unencrypted on any segment, an attacker observing the path can read member account-status information and associate closure activity with identities held by the database. The information can support targeted social engineering or account-status inference. This is conditional on the unknown transport attribute.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker needs a position on an internal path and the model leaves transport encryption unknown. Impact is medium because the flow concerns closures in `store:identity-database`, which holds member PII and credentials, although the stated payload is account-closure data.

mitigations.summary: Protect the support-console database hop with TLS
mitigations.detail: Determine the actual protocol for `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts` and require authenticated TLS for the entire hop.

claims.title: A copied identity database may expose credentials if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:identity-database` holds member email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents, while `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the unresolved attribute means storage, backups, snapshots, or decommissioned media are not encrypted, an attacker obtaining an operational copy can read credential and PII material without using `process:authorization-server`. Recovered refresh tokens or password-hash material can enable later access to authorization and rewards flows. This draft is conditional and does not assert that the store is unencrypted.

quotes.text: Nobody recorded how the rewards API connects to the ledger, how the support console connects to the identity database, or how any of the three stores is protected at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:identity-database:encryption_at_rest`: obtaining a snapshot or backup is a distinct prerequisite, but may bypass application controls. Impact is high because `store:identity-database` is tagged `credentials` and `pii` and holds reusable refresh tokens and password hashes.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the identity database and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Verify encryption at rest for `store:identity-database`, then require KMS-managed encryption for the primary store, backups, snapshots, replicas, and decommissioned media.

mitigations.summary: Constrain access to database exports and keys
mitigations.detail: Separate backup/export permissions from application access and restrict decrypt-key use to the minimal operational principals.

claims.title: A copied points ledger may disclose the complete member transaction corpus
claims.description: `store:points-ledger` contains every member balance and every points transaction, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If the store or its backups and snapshots are unencrypted, someone obtaining a storage-layer copy can read the full financial activity corpus without authenticating through `process:rewards-api`. The corpus can reveal member behavior and support targeted fraud or profiling. This is a conditional storage-copy threat pending confirmation of the at-rest control.

quotes.text: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because a storage copy must be obtained and the encryption-at-rest state is unknown. Impact is high because `store:points-ledger` contains every member's balances and transactions and is tagged `financial` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt ledger media, snapshots, and backups
mitigations.detail: Confirm and enforce encryption at rest for `store:points-ledger` and every backup, replica, and exported snapshot using managed keys with restricted decrypt permissions.

claims.title: An unencrypted API-log copy would expose replayable bearer tokens
claims.description: `store:api-log-store` contains every rewards-API request, including headers and bearer access tokens, and has unknown `encryption_at_rest`. If storage-layer encryption is absent, an attacker who obtains a backup, snapshot, or decommissioned copy can read bearer tokens and associated request data without going through `process:rewards-api`. A still-valid captured token can then be presented to the rewards API, extending the disclosure into member PII, balances, and transaction data. This is conditional on the unknown at-rest posture.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
Access tokens are signed JWTs that live for one hour, and they are plain bearer tokens.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the attacker must obtain a storage copy and `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. Impact is high because `store:api-log-store` holds bearer credentials, PII, and request data, and a captured bearer token can be used against `process:rewards-api` during its one-hour lifetime.

mitigations.summary: Remove access tokens from API logs
mitigations.detail: Redact or tokenize Authorization headers at `process:rewards-api` before `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` is emitted.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and tightly control log-store copies
mitigations.detail: Verify encryption at rest for `store:api-log-store`, cover backups and snapshots, and limit both log-reader and key-decrypt permissions.

claims.title: Weak or absent identity-database authentication could expose the credential corpus
claims.description: `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` is a read-write path for `process:authorization-server`, and its authentication attribute is unknown. If this unknown resolves to absent, weak, shared, or overly broad database authentication, an attacker who can reach the database endpoint could read the identity corpus through that path: accounts, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents in `store:identity-database`. Recovered tokens and credentials then enable follow-on access to `process:authorization-server` and `process:rewards-api`. This is conditional on the unresolved authentication control.

quotes.text: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker must reach the database endpoint and the flow authentication state is unknown. Impact is high because `store:identity-database` contains credentials and PII, including refresh tokens that can provide follow-on access.

mitigations.detail: Set a verified authentication mechanism on `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants`; use a unique workload identity, network restrictions, and grants limited to necessary rows and columns.

claims.title: Weak or absent ledger authentication could disclose all member balances
claims.description: `process:rewards-api` reads `store:points-ledger` through `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points`, whose authentication is unknown. If authentication is absent, weak, or over-broad, an attacker able to reach the ledger endpoint can read balances and points transactions directly rather than being constrained by the rewards API. That corpus enables profiling of members and targeting of financial activity. This draft is conditional on resolving the unknown database authentication state.

quotes.text: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker must be able to reach the ledger endpoint and the connection's authentication is unknown. Impact is high because `store:points-ledger` contains every member's balance and transaction history and is tagged `financial` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Require a narrowly scoped ledger workload identity
mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce strong authentication on `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points`, restrict the identity to required ledger operations, and deny direct access from other principals.
